text:
maria: heads up — we're seeing a spike of 503s from hosted inference for customer C-371. Started ~20:05 UTC. Alerts show upstream worker exits

kevin: customer says requests fail intermittently, they hit us with retries and got a lot of 500/503s. Can we get a quick triage?

maria: digging — kubectl shows a bunch of infer-runner pods restarting. getting exit code 137 and occasional SIGSEGV in logs.

sam: @maria can you paste the pod logs? suspect GPU memory pressure on the batch hotpath.

maria: logs attached (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T20:06:21Z infer-runner[pid=2487]: Allocating KV cache for seq_len=4096 tokens
2026-03-15T20:06:21Z infer-runner[pid=2487]: calling cudaMalloc 12.3GB
2026-03-15T20:06:22Z kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2487 (infer-runner) total-vm:23000000kB, anon-rss:12000000kB
2026-03-15T20:06:22Z infer-runner: exit status 137
2026-03-15T20:07:01Z infer-runner[pid=3310]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f2c1b2c sp 0x7ffd...
```

josh: exit 137 is OOM killer, but segfaults are worrying. Could be driver reset or corrupt memory state after large allocations. Any GPU coredumps or dmesg?

maria: dmesg shows `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus` and `nvidia: GPU ioctl failed, errno 12`. nvidia-smi on node shows memory full then driver reset.

kevin: ticket updated with customer — they're running many short chat requests with long prompt prefixes (avg seq 3000). Might explain huge prefix KV allocation.

sam: that matches. new optimizer pushed yesterday increased prefetch window for KV caching to improve latency for long chats. Could be miscalibrated for these workloads.

maria: reproducer on staging: spawn 30 concurrent requests with seq 3500 + batch_size 8 -> same behavior: rapid memory spike then process killed.

josh: immediate mitigations:
- route C-371 traffic to fallback model (quantized-8b)
- lower max_batch_size for the pool to 1-2
- set runtime env var INFER_KV_PREFETCH=0 for that node pool

kevin: applied fallback routing and reduced pool batch size. customer confirmed fewer errors but still occasional 503 while new pods warm.

maria: created canary job that replays customer prompt set; observed worker restart after ~45s under load.

sam: plan for patch: revert aggressive KV prefetch, add defensive check for cudaMalloc failure (fail request gracefully and trigger fallback instead of letting process continue), and add guard throttle on total_kv_bytes per-process. Will open PR.

josh: short-term ops: drain worst nodes, cordon and reprovision, and remove hot patch of the prefetch flag from prod until we ship fix. Also add node-level oom detection to autoscaler to avoid scheduling more inference pods on affected nodes.

maria: ran `kubectl logs --previous` on a crashed pod, additional output:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
what(): std::bad_alloc
[1]    2487 abort (core dumped)  ./infer-runner
```

sam: std::bad_alloc from C++ layer confirms memory exhaustion path. Segfaults are probably after driver reset, not root cause.

kevin: customer is unhappy, CS escalated. I pinged account team and opened support ticket S-2026-88 with a summary of mitigations and ETA for fix.

maria: added incident playbook note: if frequent long-prefix traffic detected, route to lower-memory variant, enforce per-tenant max_seq default 2048, and throttle prefetch windows.

josh: deploy-bot: rolled back runtime config change that enabled aggressive prefetch on prod pool rtf-7.

deploy-bot: rollback complete — config rtf-7 reverted to stable at 20:32 UTC.

sam: creating PR with three changes: revert prefetch, add cudaMalloc error path to fail fast, and add an env flag to limit max_kv_bytes. Will include unit tests + integration on staging.

maria: action items assigned:
- sam: PR and staging regression (ETA 4h)
- josh: repro node reprovision + add autoscaler guard (ETA 2h)
- kevin: CS follow-up and customer mitigation note (in progress)

kevin: updated customer: "We've routed you to a lower-memory model and adjusted our batch settings; root cause is upstream worker memory exhaustion caused by large prefix sizes. We're deploying a software rollback + fix and will confirm post-deploy"

maria: postmortem checklist: capture full stack traces, gather nvidia-smi logs for affected nodes, quantify request size distribution for C-371, and consider an automated policy to reject requests > 4096 tokens.

josh: marking P1 for now until we have PR merged and runs clean on staging. Will update this thread on status. :rotating_light:

sam: quick note for eng-runtime: this is a reminder that prefetch/backfill knobs need safety caps — pushing an explicit limit into config is low risk.

maria: thanks everyone. will keep channel updated.

kevin: closing loop: customer reported normal behavior after fallback; will monitor 24h and escalate if anything else pops up.

maria: last log pulled at 20:52 UTC, incident moving to monitoring.
